title: PSM vs CSM: Which Scrum Certification Should You Get?
dek: Choose PSM I if you want the cheaper, rigorous, no-expiry option you can self-study; choose CSM if you'd benefit from a mandatory two-day course and your employer is paying.

seo.metaTitle: PSM vs CSM: Which Scrum Certification?
seo.metaDescription: PSM vs CSM compared on 2026 cost, difficulty, course requirements, and renewal — and how to pick the right Scrum Master certification for you.

body.richText: PSM and CSM are the two best-known Scrum Master certifications, from two different organizations. They teach similar fundamentals, so the real decision comes down to cost, whether you want a mandatory course, and whether the credential expires.
Short version: paying yourself and comfortable self-studying? PSM I — cheaper, respected, and never expires. Want a structured live course and your employer foots the bill? CSM.

body.richText: The biggest practical differences: the CSM forces you to take (and pay for) a two-day course, while the PSM I lets you self-study and sit the exam for $200 — and the PSM I never expires, so there's no renewal cost over time.

body.richText: Don't pay for the CSM course out of pocket just for the brand if budget matters — the PSM I gives you a respected Scrum Master credential for a fraction of the price. Reserve the CSM for when someone else is paying.

items.question: Is PSM or CSM more respected?
items.answerRichText: Both are well recognized. Some employers view the PSM I's harder, closed-book exam as a stronger signal of knowledge, while the CSM's Scrum Alliance brand is extremely widespread. In practice, either satisfies most job requirements.

items.question: Which Scrum certification is cheaper?
items.answerRichText: PSM I, clearly — you can self-study and pay just the $200 exam fee, and it never needs renewing. The CSM requires a mandatory course, pushing the total to roughly $800–$1,500, plus renewal every two years.

items.question: Do I need a course to get a Scrum Master certification?
